query: What different themes do students raise in these open responses?

per_column.name: themes
per_column.rationale: Multi-label thematic tagging is directly the analytical axis the query asks for ('what different themes do students raise'), giving strong ability to group and compare. Samples are sound readings: ED-0001 tech_issues, ED-0004 self_paced_learning, ED-0005 engagement_loss all well grounded. Minor issue: ED-0002 tagged 'teacher_quality' is a slightly loose reading (the text is about the teacher's own experience, not quality per se), and ED-0003 'equity_access' is a mild stretch, but overall values are defensible extractions.

per_column.name: primary_theme
per_column.rationale: A single dominant theme is a useful, non-trivial reduction for ranking/prioritizing the most salient issue per response, enabling clean grouping. It partly overlaps with 'themes' but adds the analytical leverage of a chosen primary, which is a legitimate distinct axis. Selected primaries in samples (tech_issues, unexpected_success, self_paced_learning, engagement_loss) are well justified by the source text.

per_column.name: sentiment
per_column.rationale: Sentiment is a somewhat generic axis and only tangential to a 'what themes' query, but a three-way positive/mixed/negative split is more informative than a bare binary flag and can help cross-tabulate themes with tone, so it retains modest usefulness. Values are well grounded: ED-0001/0003/0005 negative, ED-0002/0004 positive all match the text.

judge.rationale: The theme and primary_theme columns squarely serve the thematic-analysis query and provide strong grouping/comparison leverage; sentiment is more generic but still adds a usable cross-cut. Row evidence shows values are sound readings of the source text with only minor interpretive stretches (e.g. teacher_quality/equity_access tags) and no invented facts, so groundedness is high.
